review_scope: Complete Chinese–English alignment read including the table, title, deck, costs, two-way coverage differences and all retained self-corrections. Six local clarifications; otherwise the complete English is retained.

changes.before: Two disagreements: auctoritas principis does not block the self-defence of the powerless — what it blocks is that a private act of defence does not automatically carry the juridical powers of public war. And supreme emergency permits cancelling the other party's carrier of cultivation to preserve one's own; SAE declines that permission and bears the cost of declining. This is registered as a ground conflict, not as internal failure.
changes.after: Two disagreements: auctoritas principis does not block the self-defence of the powerless — it prevents a private act of defence from automatically carrying the juridical powers of public war. And supreme emergency permits cancelling the other party's carrier of cultivation to preserve one's own; SAE declines that permission and bears the cost of declining. This is registered as a ground conflict, not as internal failure.
changes.reason: Clarify the negation scope: the gate blocks automatic acquisition of public-war powers, not the lack of those powers.

changes.before: So what auctoritas principis blocks is not the self-defence of the powerless. It is that a private act of defence does not automatically carry the juridical powers of public war — to initiate, to punish, to mobilise, to intend to kill. And Aquinas gives more than a slogan: a private person may not make war, because in a normal political condition he may assert his right before a superior's tribunal; nor can a private person summon the multitude that public war requires; conversely, the care of the common good is entrusted to public authority, which must repel enemies without as it uses public coercion against wrongdoers within. The substance of this gate is public jurisdiction, responsibility for the common good, and the prevention of a private quarrel being converted into public war.
changes.after: So what auctoritas principis blocks is not the self-defence of the powerless. It prevents a private act of defence from automatically carrying the juridical powers of public war — to initiate, to punish, to mobilise, to intend to kill. The substance of this gate is public jurisdiction, responsibility for the common good, and the prevention of a private quarrel being converted into public war.
changes.reason: Match the corrected abstract and avoid reversing what legitimate authority blocks.

changes.before: The distance is smaller than it is usually taken to be, and that must be acknowledged. The four gates on the second face of Theorem One — do not open the second face on its own; see without substituting; genuine rising; the intervening party must have interests of its own — block the same class of things. An armed body claiming to represent the oppressed with no one having asked it fails the third gate; an intervener with no connection to the party intervened for fails the fourth; an action packaging a private quarrel as liberation fails the first. Aquinas's reasons are the same class of reason as what the four gates exist to prevent. To say that SAE rejects legitimate authority and is therefore more permissive is inaccurate.
changes.after: The distance is smaller than it is usually taken to be, and that must be acknowledged. An armed body claiming to represent the oppressed with no one having asked it fails the third gate; an intervener with no connection to the party intervened for fails the fourth; an action packaging a private quarrel as liberation fails the first. Aquinas's reasons address the same class of danger that the four gates exist to prevent. To say that SAE rejects legitimate authority and is therefore more permissive is inaccurate.
changes.reason: Repair a category mismatch between reasons and dangers without changing the claimed overlap.

changes.before: The argument: the bridge clause prohibits foreclosing the other party's possibility of reorganising itself as a subject of cultivation — and what supreme emergency asks to exempt is precisely that class of means; it exempts what is ordinarily forbidden, which is to say the most thorough. So the content of the exception is: when one party's carrier of cultivation is threatened, the other's may be cancelled. And that cannot be uttered within SAE, for a reason of the same form as volume two's: cultivation cannot authorise its own cancellation. A criterion in the name of preserving cultivation whose content is cancelling the other party's cultivation cancels the condition of its own standing. It has not violated a rule; it does not obtain.
changes.after: The argument: the bridge clause prohibits foreclosing the other party's possibility of reorganising itself as a subject of cultivation — and what supreme emergency asks to exempt is precisely that class of means; it exempts what is ordinarily forbidden, which is to say the most thorough. So the content of the exception is: when one party's carrier of cultivation is threatened, the other's may be cancelled. And that cannot be uttered within SAE, for a reason of the same form as volume two's: cultivation cannot authorise the cancellation of cultivation. A criterion in the name of preserving cultivation whose content is cancelling the other party's cultivation cancels the condition of its own standing. It has not violated a rule; it does not obtain.
changes.reason: Do not narrow the principle to cancellation of one’s own cultivation; the argument explicitly concerns the other party’s carrier.

changes.before: But the cost must be acknowledged, and the acknowledgement cannot be formal. Walzer's exception was not set down carelessly; it answers to a real situation — there are moments at which keeping the rules may mean the destruction of a community. SAE's refusal of the exception is the bearing of that cost: it issues no exception clause available to be invoked at such a moment, and a community in that situation gets no dispensation from SAE. That bearing must be written down; the situation may not be pretended away. And what SAE bears it on must also be written: not that the situation will not arise, but that once the exception is established, any party may claim to stand at that tier, and no one has standing to verify the claim.

changes.before: Theorem One does not ask whether this war is just. It asks: has the carrier of cultivation been lost; can cultivation in its mild forms no longer continue; do the four gates pass. These are judgements about structure, requiring not standing but sight.
changes.after: Theorem One does not ask whether this war is just. It asks: has the carrier of cultivation been lost; can cultivation in its mild forms no longer continue; have the four gates been passed. These are judgements about structure, requiring not standing but sight.
changes.reason: The case passes the gates, not the gates themselves.

metadata_changes.before: The four theorems are most easily read as a new just war theory. This volume exists to prevent that misreading: SAE does not establish the adjudicating position — and Grotius stands on the same side.
metadata_changes.after: The four theorems are most easily read as a new just war theory. This volume exists to prevent that misreading: SAE does not establish the position from which to determine who is the just party — and Grotius stands on the same side.
metadata_changes.reason: Restore the specific object of the adjudication in the deck.
